M03.title: Robot and terrain visual
approvedFacts: Recorded foothold-v2 terrain clips exist with per-clip capture metadata (policy sha256, camera, seed, command speed).
The NVIDIA checkpoint, foothold-v1, and foothold-v2 are distinct policies and must be captioned as such.
prohibitedClaims: A pictured frame shows a physical Go2 running a FOOTHOLD policy.
A pictured policy is captioned without naming which policy it is.
The pictured terrain is the team's final target terrain.
requiredEvidence: Choose one frame and copy it, with its capture metadata, into an approved location in this repository.
Record provenance, capture date, policy, terrain, and the licence status of the rendered robot model before Figma import.

M04.title: Sim-to-Real flow
approvedFacts: Verified: the NVIDIA Isaac-Velocity-Rough-Unitree-Go2-v0 checkpoint is the baseline policy (decision 2026-09-02).
Verified: foothold-v1 (released 2026-09-11) and foothold-v2 (released 2026-09-29) were trained from that checkpoint; both files carry sha256 records.
Verified: the unseen-terrain generalization evaluation and the MVP report were delivered for the 2026-09-30 gate.
Decided 2026-10-12: the FOOTHOLD RL policy is not deployed to the physical Go2. Track B runs the stock gait with SLAM and Nav2.
Planned: the SIM gate (2026-11-07) and the NAV gate (2026-11-30).
prohibitedClaims: FOOTHOLD has completed sim-to-real deployment.
The FOOTHOLD RL policy runs on the physical Go2.
The exported ONNX policy has been validated on a physical Go2.
requiredEvidence: Show verified and planned stages with different semantic states.
Promote each planned stage only after a reproducible run record exists.

M05.title: Why FOOTHOLD
approvedFacts: The approved brand problem statement may be used.
The project scope is a terrain-adaptive quadruped locomotion policy, not a navigation platform.
시뮬레이터에서 천 번 넘어지고, 현장에서는 넘어지지 않는다. is approved as the target vision for the intended Sim-to-Real outcome.
The target vision must remain explicitly labelled TARGET VISION until reproducible physical-field evidence supports promotion.
prohibitedClaims: Formal deployment partners or field operations exist.
The project already protects people in deployed environments.
The target-vision sentence is a current verified zero-fall result or a measured field-performance claim.
requiredEvidence: Approve one concrete use context without naming an unconfirmed partner.
Separate intended benefit from demonstrated outcome.
Preserve reproducible physical test conditions and fall-rate results before changing TARGET VISION to a verified outcome.

M06.title: Evidence
approvedFacts: On eight terrains that no policy trained on (3 speeds, 100 episodes per cell, difficulty 0.5, eval spec 2, seed 42), the NVIDIA checkpoint scores 43.88 % and foothold-v2 scores 88.46 % (recomputed from the per-episode raw files: 43.875 % and 88.458 %, 2,400 episodes each).
Success requires survival, progress, tracking, and direction to all pass.
stepping_stones at 1.0 m/s reads 24, 1, 3, 19, and 0 of 100 across five seeds, so it is quoted as 0 to 24 %.
All results are simulation results. No FOOTHOLD RL policy result on the physical Go2 exists or is planned (decision 2026-10-12).
prohibitedClaims: 21,385 steps/s is a measured training result.
1,500 training iterations take approximately 113 minutes in the verified setup.
Any physical-robot success rate, fall rate, or deployment result for a FOOTHOLD policy.
foothold-v2 is better than foothold-v1 (the +1.75 %p difference is the same size as seed-to-seed variation).
stepping_stones reaches 24 % without the 0 to 24 % range.
Each terrain was tested on 100 different terrain instances (the 100 episodes share one tile).
gap or rails results count as unseen-terrain generalization.
requiredEvidence: Quote every number with its evaluation conditions and raw-file path.
Recompute a number from the per-episode raw files before promoting it.
Run training before publishing training throughput or duration.
